prompt: A hiker walks 300 m north in 240 s and then 400 m east in 360 s. Which row gives the average speed and the magnitude and direction of the average velocity for the complete journey?
options: average speed 0.833 m s^-1; average velocity 0.833 m s^-1 at 53.1 degrees east of north
average speed 1.17 m s^-1; average velocity 0.833 m s^-1 at 53.1 degrees east of north
average speed 1.17 m s^-1; average velocity 0.667 m s^-1 east
average speed 0.833 m s^-1; average velocity 1.17 m s^-1 at 36.9 degrees north of east

answer.explanation: Total distance = 700 m and total time = 600 s, so average speed = 1.17 m s^-1. Resultant displacement = 500 m at 53.1 degrees east of north, so average velocity = 500/600 = 0.833 m s^-1 in the same direction. B is correct.

distractor_explanations: Option 1 incorrectly uses the displacement magnitude to calculate average speed.

Option 2 is correct: total distance = 300 + 400 = 700 m, total time = 240 + 360 = 600 s, average speed = 700 / 600 = 1.17 m s^-1. Resultant displacement = sqrt(300^2 + 400^2) = 500 m. Average velocity = 500 / 600 = 0.833 m s^-1 at tan^-1(400/300) = 53.1 degrees east of north.
Option 3 omits the angle of displacement and gives velocity purely east.
Option 4 inverts the speed and velocity values and gives the complementary angle north of east.
hints: Use total path length for average speed. Use the straight-line resultant for average velocity.
The north and east legs form a 3-4-5 right triangle. Total time is 240 + 360 s.
solution: Total distance = 700 m and total time = 600 s, so average speed = 1.17 m s^-1. Resultant displacement = 500 m at 53.1 degrees east of north, so average velocity = 500/600 = 0.833 m s^-1 in the same direction. B is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Add the route lengths for distance: 300 m + 400 m = 700 m.
Add the stage times: 240 s + 360 s = 600 s.
Average speed = 700 m / 600 s = 1.17 m s^-1.
For displacement, draw the 300 m north and 400 m east vectors head-to-tail. The straight start-to-finish line is the hypotenuse.
Measured east of north, tan(theta) = 400/300, so theta = 53.1 degrees.
Average velocity magnitude = 500 m / 600 s = 0.833 m s^-1. Its direction is 53.1 degrees east of north. Therefore B is correct.
